name: Mr. D Math
line: Mr. D Math teaches by video lesson, worksheet and quiz. In AMP, assessment and teaching happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Mr. D Math: Mr. D Math teaches by video lesson, worksheet and quiz. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Mr. D Math teaches in lessons: a recorded video, a worksheet the student checks against a key, then a computer-graded quiz, in the course's order [4][7]. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous. Every answer is checked and explained at once, updates the learner's level and sets the next problem.

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In Mr. D Math the unit is the lesson. The student watches a recorded lesson, works a worksheet of about 20 questions, checks it against the solution key, then takes a quiz [4]. In an online psychology course for adults, students who did more interactive activities learned more than students who watched more video or read more. The data are correlational [10].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After every answer, AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. In a self-paced Mr. D Math lesson, the student works the whole worksheet, then checks it against the solution key [4]. The keys show each step, color-coded to help find errors [5].

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. In a Mr. D Math course, assessment is the computer-graded quizzes, tests and exams set along the way [7].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Mr. D Math builds review into each course as set assignments: spiral reviews, mid-chapter reviews, chapter tests and semester exams [4][7]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [11].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP an answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped. A skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once, and repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. A Mr. D Math student moves to the next lesson on the course's pace chart, or at the instructor's pace in a live course [7][8]. Quizzes may be retaken with notes, and a student who is stuck can join a live help session [3][6].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math and runs from counting through precalculus in one program. A learner further along in geometry than in fractions gets work at both levels. Mr. D Math works one course at a time, from 5th Grade Math through Calculus I, and the family picks the course with a course-selection guide [3][7][9].

rows.range: Single courses from 5th Grade Math through Calculus I, plus Statistics and Consumer Math [2][7][9].
rows.start: The family picks the course, with a course-selection guide linked from its FAQ [3].
rows.teaching: A recorded video lesson, then a worksheet of about 20 questions. Live courses add one Zoom class a week [4][8].
rows.next: The next lesson in the course, on a 34-week pace chart, or at the instructor's pace in a live course [7][8].
rows.mastery: Grades from computer-graded quizzes, tests and exams [7]. Quizzes may be retaken with notes [6].
rows.review: Spiral reviews, mid-chapter reviews, chapter tests and semester exams, set in the course [4][7].
rows.print: Worksheets and answer keys printed from the course, or a printed binder. We found no version made for each student [3][4][5].
rows.adult: Prints worksheets and may check work against the keys. In live courses, instructors grade assigned work [4][5].
rows.reports: Computer-graded quiz, test and exam scores [7].

theirs: Mr. D Math is an online math school for grades 5 to 12, run by the teacher Dennis DiNoia [1][12]. Its math courses run from 5th Grade Math through Calculus I, with Statistics and Consumer Math beside them [2][7][9]. Each course comes self-paced or live, and in a gamified or a traditional version [8].

A self-paced lesson goes in four steps: watch the recorded lesson, work a worksheet of about 20 questions, check it against the solution key, then take a computer-graded quiz [4]. A self-paced student follows a pace chart through the course [7]. A live student also joins one Zoom class a week, and instructors grade assigned work [5][8].
credit: A teacher explains each lesson on video, and live students meet an instructor every week [4][8].
Live help sessions every week for a student who is stuck [3].
Answer keys show every step, color-coded to help a student find an error [5].

theirs: We found no outcome study of Mr. D Math on its site [1].
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. In an online psychology course for adults, students who did more interactive activities learned more than students who watched more video or read more pages. The authors put the benefit of extra doing at more than six times that of extra watching or reading, in data that are correlational [10]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [11]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: You want a teacher on video, a weekly live class and live help sessions.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want every answer checked and explained the moment it is given.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math.
You want workbooks made for your learner, with worked answer keys.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Mr. D Math?
questions.answer: Mr. D Math teaches by recorded lesson, then a worksheet checked against a key, then a quiz, in the course's order [4][7]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Mr. D Math work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of Mr. D Math on its site [1].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers and chooses practice from there.
